body:
WHAT
The system prompt sent on every request is composed from nine behaviour sections (identity, harness, communication, action care, git, code style, tasks, working method, autonomy), then an environment block (cwd, git repo, platform, model, date), then an addons roster when addons exist, then any extra sections (OVERDRIVE, deletion policy, subagent role). Each section is defined once as an exported constant and registered as a prompt so it can be edited or switched off; a disabled section is dropped without leaving a blank gap.

WHY
Without a single ordered assembly point sections could be duplicated, drift, or be joined in the wrong order, and an embedding frontend could not swap or drop one cleanly.

WHERE
engine/core/src/agent/prompts.ts — SECTION_IDENTITY, SECTION_HARNESS, SECTION_COMMUNICATION, SECTION_ACTION_CARE, SECTION_GIT, SECTION_CODE_STYLE, SECTION_TASKS, SECTION_WORKING_METHOD, SECTION_AUTONOMY; CORE_SECTIONS registry; behaviorCore(); environmentBlock() / ENVIRONMENT_BLOCK; addonsBlock() / ADDONS_BLOCK; buildSystemPrompt({env, addons, extraSections}). Callers: engine/core/src/runtime/session.ts — Session.buildSystemPrompt() and Session.spawnAgent().

TEST CHECKLIST
1. buildSystemPrompt({env}) with no addons contains each of the nine SECTION_* texts exactly once, in registry order (identity index < harness index < … < autonomy index), followed by 'Environment:' with the given cwd/platform/model/date.
2. With addons [{name:'x', description:'d'}] the output contains 'Available addons' and '- x: d' after the environment block; with an empty array it contains no 'Available addons' text.
3. extraSections ['ROLE', 'CONTRACT'] appear at the end, in that order, after the environment/addons blocks.
4. Disabling one section prompt (e.g. 'system.git' emptied in the registry) removes SECTION_GIT text from behaviorCore() and leaves no double blank line (no '\n\n\n') in the result.
5. The identity section renders PRODUCT_NAME/PRODUCT_REPO_URL placeholders (the output contains 'Magentra' and the repo URL, no literal '{{product}}').
